range.remark: Pss 41-46 (end of Book I, start of Book II); Ps 47 intro begins pdf 343, notes -> next batch

entries.note: LXX add καὶ πένητα, i.e. ואביון, as Ps 72:13, 82:4, 1 Sam 2:8 — terms synonymous with עני/ענו, the circle of the sufferers (p. 24 f.). משכיל אל/על = 'attend to, care about someone'. The blessing vv. 2b–4 is the well-wisher's implied speech, with לאמר to be understood (as Ps 40:5).

entries.emendation: Keri יְאֻשַּׁר; ואל תתנהו → ואל יתנהו (3rd person)
entries.note: The Keri יאשר is more correct than the Kethib. בארץ without qualifier = 'in the homeland' Judea (cf. Ps 37:3) — the sick sufferer shall share the happiness promised the exiles on their return. For ואל תתנהו LXX, Symmachus and Pesh. have the third person (καὶ μὴ παραδῴη αὐτόν), 'viel richtiger' (interchange of personal affixes, p. 135, 17).

כל משכבו הפכת בחליו is inexplicable with all arts of interpretation. Leg. על (כ miswritten for ע, p. 134, 14): על משכבו = על ערש דוי, and before הפכת supply the relative אשר: 'auf seinem Lager, das Du in seiner Krankheit verwandelt'.
'Heal my soul, for I have sinned against Thee' is a strange motivation of the plea; leg. כי קראתי לך (interchange of ק and ח, p. 126, 6): 'heile meine Seele, denn ich rufe Dich an!'
While the singer pleads for healing his enemies say רע לי — vielleicht leg. לו, 'weh’ ihm!' ('Meine Feinde aber sprachen: weh’ ihm! wann wird er sterben').

entries.mt: וְאִם־בָּא לִרְאוֹת שָׁוְא יְדַבֵּר לִבּוֹ יִקְבָּץ־אָוֶן לוֹ יֵצֵא לַחוּץ יְדַבֵּר
entries.emendation: plural throughout: ואם באו לראות שוא ידברו, לבם יקבץ און לי, יצאו לחוץ ידברו (יחד עלי drawn from v. 8)
entries.note: V. 7 is conspicuous by its incongruence — before and after, the enemies are plural. Pesh. has the plural, and LXX join יחד (עלי) of v. 8 to v. 7; one cannot say יצא לחוץ ידבר יחד עלי, so the verbs must be plural. Vv. 7–8 should run: ואם באו לראות שוא ידברו / לבם יקבץ און לי / יצאו לחוץ ידברו יחד עלי // יתלחשו כל שנאי עלי / יחשבו רעה לי. אין = עמל 'mischief'; לי of course statt לו. This also explains the heaping of עלי/לי in v. 8.

entries.emendation: supply אמרו before the quote; ואשר → באשר
entries.note: יצוק = 'firmly cast, fixed' (so rightly Hengstenberg and Delitzsch; frequent in Job), so דבר בליעל can only mean moral depravity — the enemies' malicious talk against the psalmist; אמרו must be supplied. And ואשר שכב is inexplicable in the Masoretic form; leg. באשר, the ב softened to ו (p. 122): 'da, wo er liegt, auf dem Siechbette'.

entries.emendation: הגדיל עלי עקבו (draw the ו of ואתה)
entries.note: הגדיל עלי עקב is obscure; עקב seems to mean 'ambush, treachery' here (Josh 8:13), with the ו of the following ואתה drawn to it: הגדיל עלי עקבו, like הרבה: 'vermehrt seine Hinterlist gegen mich'. אוכל לחמי must, for symmetry, be a predicate like הגדיל עלי, hence figurative: 'slander, accuse' (p. 194).

חנני vielfach leg. חיני, as often in Ps 119: 'lass mich genesen'. And ואשלמה is difficult — absolutely it could at best mean 'requite good', but without טוב it stays ambiguous; daher wohl leg. ושלמה imperative (addressed to God): 'richte mich auf und vergilt ihnen'.
entries.flag: verify both proposed forms (חיני, ושלמה) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Since the psalm always speaks of several enemies, the clause must be made congruent: יריעו איבי (plural): 'wenn meine Feinde nicht triumphiren über mich'.

תמכת בי is unintelligible: transitive תמך governs the accusative, and with ב it means to hold fast to someone — which cannot be said of God. Daher leg. תמכתי, first person with בתמי, 'I hold fast to my integrity' (Job 2:3, 9 מחזיק בתמתו; 27:6). The following בי leg. כי, joined to the verb: כי תציבני (the ו of ותציבני dittographed from בי): 'Ich aber halte an meiner Schlichtheit fest, Du haltest mich vor Dir für immer aufrecht'.

The two psalms' belonging together is so striking that it did not escape the ancients — Eusebius already remarks on Ps 43 that by identity of style and train of thought it clearly forms part of Ps 42 (shared refrain, shared למה קדר אתהלך בלחץ אויב). Together they form one lament of a Levite singer banished from the sanctuary — pre-exilic, at the foot of Hermon by the Jordan springs, under Manasseh's persecution.
בֶּאֱמֹר אלי leg. באמרם, as v. 11: 'wenn sie zu mir alle Tage sprechen: Wo ist Dein Gott?' — spoken by opponents still in the homeland, before the banishment.

entries.mt: אֶעֱבֹר בַּסָּךְ אֶדַּדֵּם עַד־בֵּית אֱלֹהִים … הָמוֹן חוֹגֵג
entries.emendation: אעבר בסוד מְשֹׁרְרִים עד בית אלהים … המון חוגגים
entries.note: בסך אדדם is inexplicable despite all arts of interpretation: סך 'multitude' is hapax (Aramaic סך = 'sum', not crowd), and אֶדַּדֵּם is formally an 'Unwort'. Statt בסך leg. בסוד (interchange ד/ך, p. 129, 1) — the intimate circle is called סוד (סוד משחקים, סוד ישרים, סוד בחורים); in the corrupted אדדם must lurk the second member of the construct, a substantive — משוררים suggests itself most readily (interchange of ש/מ, p. 150; רר corrupted to דד, ש dropped): 'wie ich im Kreise der Sänger zu Gottes Tempel zog'. This fits the close: for המון חוגג LXX and Symmachus have the plural ἑορταζόντων = חוגגים (the ם absorbed by the following מה), apposition to סוד משוררים — a reminiscence of the festal processions of Hezekiah's time.

entries.emendation: read all three times ישועת פני אלהי
entries.note: The refrain occurring three times must of course read identically and the variant be eliminated. ידה governs a double accusative (person and thing): אודנו ישועת can only mean 'thank God for the help (of His countenance)'; פני = the friendly face, goodwill. So read all three times ישועת פני אלהי — statt פניו; the ו of ואלהי dittographed from the י, and in the first occurrence אלהי dropped out: 'für die Gunstwendung meines Gottes'.

Two or more 'Hermons' do not exist (despite Jerome's fable of a little Hermon); rightly Pesh. מן חרמון — the ים is evidently dittographed from the following מ of מהר. And הר מצער 'the little mountain' is suspect — where would it lie? The Hermon was from of old a cult mountain (בעל גד / בעל חרמון, Josh 11:17, 1 Chr 5:23; in Greek times the Paneion, Banias); such a mountain of festal assembly is הר מועד (Isa 14:13). Reading מהר מועד (letter confusion), the phrase is simply apposition to חרמון: 'vom Hermon, dem Festwallberg'.

entries.mt: יוֹמָם יְצַוֶּה יְהוָה חַסְדּוֹ וּבַלַּיְלָה שִׁירֹה עִמִּי תְּפִלָּה לְאֵל חַיָּי
entries.emendation: supply אקרא with יומם; שירה → שִׂיחָה; לאל חיי → לאל חי
entries.note: The verse is not really intelligible: יומם (a) and בלילה (b) are parallel, and something contained in b must be supplied with יומם — roughly אקרא (as Ps 22:3). In b, תפלה and שירה must be synonymous; leg. שיחה 'complaint, plaint'. And statt לאל חיי leg. לאל חי, as v. 3: 'Tags (rufe ich): möge der Herr seine Gnade entbieten, und Nachts ist bei mir die Klage, ein Gebet zum lebendigen Gott'.
למה שכחתני vielleicht leg. למה זנחתני as 43:2; but in any case statt אלך leg. אתהלך as there ('warum soll ich düster einhergehen bei des Frevlers Druck?').

ברצח בעצמותי is unintelligible; leg. כרקב 'like rot in my bones', as Prov 12:4, 14:30 (interchange of צ/ק and ח/ב, pp. 127, 8; 131, 3i). But the verb חרפוני then does not fit; leg. חרפות צררי 'the taunts of my foes' (interchange of ־וני and ־ות): 'Wie Moder in meinem Gebein, so die Lästerung der Höhner'.

שמחת גילי is pleonasm, leg. שמחת לבי 'the joy of my heart'. And אלהים אלהי is striking; leg. אלהים אל חי as Ps 42:3 (interchange of ה and ח, p. 126, 6b): 'Gott, lebendiger Gott' — the Levite singer longing to play the harp in the Temple again (v. 3 אורך ואמתך = the Urim and Thummim).

ותטעם has been misunderstood by the interpreters (assuming another object); leg. ותסעם 'uproot' (interchange of ט and ס). תרע is mostly construed with ל, so leg. ללאמים (the ל absorbed). And for ותשלחם LXX ἐξέβαλες, i.e. ותשליכם (p. 196, 7): 'vertrieben und entwurzelt, geschädigt Stämme und sie verbannt'.

entries.emendation: a form of גוח 'fight' (Aramaic אגחא קרבא)
entries.note: Hebrew נגח means only 'gore with the horns', which does not fit here. It is wohl the Aramaic גוח / אגח, which also means 'fight' (אגחא קרבא); cf. Dan 11:40 ויתגח. Daher leg. the corresponding form: 'Mit Dir werden wir unsere Gegner bekriegen'.
entries.flag: verify proposed form (נגיח/נגוח?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: V. 10 forms the transition — אך זנחת, but unrecognizable because of אף (p. 129f). LXX have in addition νυνί, Pesh. השא, i.e. עתה, which makes the construction more pregnant: אך עתה זנחת (parallel Ps 89:39 ואתה זנחת): 'Aber jetzt hast Du verlassen und uns beschämt'.
רבית as Piel of רבה is doubtful; leg. הרבית Hiphil: 'und erwarbst nichts bei ihrem Kaufpreis'.

For מקול leg. מפי (cf. Ps 8:3, p. 140). מתנקם, intensive of נקם 'breathing vengeance', refers to Antiochus Epiphanes, as does מחרף ומגדף — he blasphemed God (1 Macc 1:24; Dan 7:25, 8:11) and wrought a bloodbath in Judea from vengefulness (the psalm is Maccabean; John Hyrcanus removed it from the Temple liturgy, Geschichte der Juden III, p. 120).
entries.flag: verify lemma/emendation (מקול→מפי?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: כי is concessive, 'obwohl'. For דכיתנו leg. דחיתנו 'thrust us away' ('Obwohl Du uns verstossen in Stätten von Ungethümen'); תנים is shortened from תנינים — place of monsters = wilderness, attested by 1 Macc 1:53, 2:29–31 (the pious fleeing to the desert).

entries.mt: רָחַשׁ לִבִּי דָּבָר טוֹב אֹמֵר אָנִי מַעֲשַׂי לְמֶלֶךְ
entries.note: רחש is not quite secure (Hebrew otherwise only in מרחשת; Aramaic it means 'swarm, crawl' — 'bubble forth' is only guessed); דבר טוב is quite unseemly, and אמר אני מעשי barely graspable (hardly ᾔρξατο as all the Greek versions). In short, half-verse a is unclear — his translation marks 'mein Gedicht (?)'.

יפיפית is to be divided יפה יפית ('Schön, schöner bist du als Menschensöhne'). הוצק חן בשפתותיך can only mean possessing graceful, well-set speech, 'poetic eloquence' — the addressed king (Hezekiah, to whom the psalm is dated) must have been a poet.

entries.emendation: על ירכך (with suffix, per LXX); supply היא before הודך והדרך
entries.note: LXX and other versions read על ירך with the suffix (ἐπὶ τὸν μηρόν σου) = על ירכך. The half-verse b seems too short; supply היא: היא הודך והדרך 'es ist dein Schmuck und deine Zier'.

entries.emendation: delete והדרך (dittograph); צלח → (vielleicht) הֵחָלֵץ; וענוה צדק → וענוה וצדק
entries.note: The word והדרך is missing in LXX and Pesh. — it is dittographed (from v. 4). צלחה is unclear: Kal means 'cross over' (= עבר), which does not fit; vielleicht leg. חלץ in Niphal, 'rüste dich' ('Brich auf'). רכב 'ride', figuratively 'rule'. And וענוה צדק — an unclear compound as construct; the Greek versions have וצדק, so leg. וענוה וצדק (ענוה the virtue of the Anawim; Zeph 2:3): 'für das Wort der Wahrheit, der Milde und Gerechtigkeit'.
עמים תחתיך יפלו with the following בלב is awkward; leg. יפלו … כל איבי המלך: 'werfen Völker unter Dir nieder, alle Feinde des Königs'.

אלהים אלהיך is dittographed. And מחברך is unintelligible, especially in the singular (per the Masora), which cannot be a superlative; leg. ויבחרך, cf. Isa 49:7 קדש ישראל ויבחרך 'He has preferred, chosen you' — fitting Hezekiah, who as a younger son reached the throne (anointing occurred precisely at contested successions): 'darum salbte dich Gott mit Jubel-Oel und erwählte dich'.

כל בגדתיך is certainly corrupt, since the plural of בגד is exclusively בגדים; wohl leg. a word for 'treasuries/costly things' — his translation 'deine Gewürzkammern (?)'. And מני שמחוך can no more be a stringed instrument here than a preposition — why lyre-playing at a coronation rather than horns and flutes? Vielleicht leg. a word for songs/music ('aus dem Palast von Elfenbein erfreuen dich Lieder').
entries.flag: verify both proposed words (גנזיך? מנגינות?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Over the reading ביקרותיך the Masoretes themselves disagreed (cf. Norzi, מנחת שי ad loc.); gewiss leg. לקראתך: 'Königstöchter kommen dir entgegen'. And בכתם אופיר wahrscheinlich leg. בכתר אופיר 'with the crown of Ophir', as Song 5:11 כתם פז leg. כתר (Dan 10:5 likewise corrupt). שגל is the legitimate queen (Neh 2:6).
Pesh. more correctly ברתי, i.e. בתי — the psalmist addresses the queen familiarly, 'meine Tochter'. ושכחי עמך: עם here means not 'people' but 'family' (Monatsschrift 1874, p. 1 f.).

entries.mt: וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִי־לוֹ׃ וּבַת־צֹר בְּמִנְחָה פָּנַיִךְ יְחַלּוּ עֲשִׁירֵי עָם
entries.emendation: והשתחוו לך בנות צור במנחה / פניך יחלו עשירי עם (עמי הארץ) בכל כבודם
entries.note: כי הוא אדניך gives no intelligible motivation — a small lacuna seems to be in v. 12. LXX draw והשתחוי לו to the following verse, in the plural (καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτῷ θυγατέρες Τύρου), and Pesh. similarly repeats the verb at v. 13; LXX also begin half-verse b with פניך יחלו. Keeping this, reading לך statt לו, and drawing כל כבודה of v. 14 to v. 13 as בכל כבודם (ם/ה interchange, p. 132), vv. 12–13 take an unforced shape: the verse enumerates all who will do homage to the queen — Tyre's daughters (colonies) and the richest of the peoples with all their wealth. בת צר is thus not vocative — no Tyrian princess, still less Hitzig's Cleopatra.

entries.mt: כָּל־כְּבוּדָּה בַת־מֶלֶךְ פְּנִימָה מִמִּשְׁבְּצוֹת זָהָב לְבוּשָׁהּ
entries.emendation: בת מלך פנינים במשבצות זהב לבושה
entries.note: בת מלך is not the addressed queen — she was no princess but a commoner raised by her beauty (v. 12), addressed simply as בתי (v. 11) — but an actual king's daughter, subject of vv. 14–15 (hence אחריה v. 15; otherwise it would be אחריך). פנימה 'into the interior' gives no sense; leg. פנינים 'corals/pearls' (so also Krochmal; cf. פניים Prov 3:15), and ממשבצות leg. במשבצות: her adornment as she is led to the queen — 'Die Königstochter mit Perlen, in goldner Einfassung ihr Gewand'. (כל כבודה goes to v. 13 as בכל כבודם.)

entries.emendation: ברקמות (joined to לבושה); למלך → לְמוּלֵךְ 'dir entgegen'
entries.note: Nearly all the Greek versions connect לרקמות with לבושה, reading ברקמות 'in embroideries'. And תובל למלך 'led to the king'? The address is to the queen! Daher leg. 'toward you' — the king's daughter with her virgin companions is led to the queen as companion-servants. Vv. 14–15: בת מלך פנינים במשבצות זהב לבושה ברקמות / תובל למולך בתולות אחריה רעותיה מובאות לך.
entries.flag: verify the emended word for למלך (למולך?) at high res

entries.mt: תַּחַת אֲבֹתֶיךָ יִהְיוּ בָנֶיךָ תְּשִׁיתֵמוֹ לְשָׂרִים
entries.emendation: feminine forms: תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך תשיתימו — addressed to the queen
entries.note: V. 17 has been utterly misunderstood as an address to the king, whereas it continues the address to the queen — so Pesh. with feminine forms (בניכי, אבהיכי); the punctuators mistook the gender and misled the interpreters. Only addressed to the queen does the prospect make sense: she cannot forget her father's house — well, in its stead she will see sons as princes in all the land. (For the king, what would תחת אבתיך even mean?)

entries.mt: אַזְכִּירָה שִׁמְךָ בְּכָל־דֹּר וָדֹר עַל־כֵּן עַמִּים יְהוֹדוּךָ
entries.emendation: בניך יזכירו שמך …; על כן → עד כי
entries.note: Remarkably LXX have for the first person singular the third plural μνησθήσονται (Alexandrinus + καὶ ἀντιλήψονται), Pesh. passive דנתדכר שמך — the continuation of the address to the queen: בניך יזכירו שמך, her sons perpetuating her name through the generations (interchange of personal prefixes, p. 130, 17). In b, על כן is not quite correct: the Masoretes already noted interchange of על and עד (Monatsschrift 1881, p. 218 f.), and כן stands not seldom for כי (p. 133, 10); leg. עד כי עמים יהודוך לעולם ועד 'so that peoples will praise you for ever'.

נמצא 'findable' — who lets Himself be found by eager seeking (Jer 29:14) — but נמצא מאד is odd; leg. תמיד, Pesh. בכל זמן (frequent confusion of מאד and תמיד; cf. Ps 112:1 חפץ מאד leg. תמיד): 'Hilfe in Nöthen, findbar stets'.
בהמיר as transitive of מור 'change' with ארץ as accusative (Olshausen) is possible; besser בהמס ארץ 'when the earth melts' (Krochmal) — his translation 'wenn die Erde schmilzt'.

entries.emendation: supply the refrain ה׳ צבאות עמנו משגב לנו אלהי יעקב סלה
entries.note: The psalm has three strophes of four verses each with the same refrain; before סלה of v. 4 the refrain — which forms the fourth verse — has been effaced and must be supplied (Hupfeld). His translation prints it in parentheses. (In v. 4 מימיו: the suffix cannot refer to ימים, so either read בלב ים singular or take ימים as collective; בגאותו refers to God.)

נהר פלגיו is an impossible construction, and even a construct state would not help much, since the predicate ישמחו is plural; to be read as a verb, Hiphil הנהיר, with the ה absorbed by the preceding סלה: 'Er liess Seine Bäche strömen, dass sie erfreuen die Gottesstadt'. קדש משכני = superlative, the holiest of God's dwelling-places.

מטו ממלכות can only mean 'the kingdoms sank', so המו must be synonymous, as LXX and Pesh. render passively (ἐταράχθησαν, אשתגשו) 'were thrown into confusion' — thus a Pual form of המם, regularly הממו, shortened המו with dagesh in the מ: 'Verwirrt wurden die Nationen, es sanken die Reiche'.

'Devastations' God did not work then — on the contrary, He destroyed the instruments of devastation (v. 10). שמות is surely corrupt: the syllable שמ is dittographed from שם. LXX τέρατα, Pesh. 'wonder-signs'; folglich leg. שם אותות statt שמות: 'wie er Wunder gethan im Lande' — most naturally the sudden destruction of Sennacherib's army in Hezekiah's time.
